html:
SMTO-FIL-0063 — SMTO can't safely open that file inside the compressed file

GUID: b56aac02-b30b-5649-85ec-59d648f7002d
Slug: attachment-archive-member-unavailable
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: attachments

What happened

  • The item SMTO chose is a folder, doesn't exist, or is blocked for safety, for example because it's password-protected, a shortcut (link), or has a path pointing outside the compressed file. SMTO didn't unpack it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to list the compressed file again and choose a regular file, not a folder or an entry marked blocked. SMTO can open only ordinary files that pass its safety checks.
  2. If the file you need is password-protected, unpack it on your own computer and attach that file directly. SMTO can't open password-protected entries inside a ZIP.
  3. If the compressed file contains links or unusual paths, re-create it from plain files and attach the new copy. SMTO blocks links and paths that could point outside the compressed file.

What success looks like

  • SMTO opens the file and uses its contents in its answer.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the compressed file's name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't type the file's password into the conversation.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The requested archive member index is out of range, is a directory, or is blocked by safety checks (encrypted ZIP entry, symlink or non-regular TAR entry, absolute path, drive letter or '..' traversal); nothing was extracted.

What this means

  • The member index is absent, the row is a directory, or safety checks block encrypted content, links, traversal or absolute paths. No unsafe member is extracted. Diagnostic presentation does not grant access, change task configuration or establish the outcome of earlier operations.

Why this can happen

  • The member index is absent, the row is a directory, or safety checks block encrypted content, links, traversal or absolute paths. No unsafe member is extracted.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact error kind and retained source or route receipt. Distinguish a rejected reference from an authorized source whose bytes cannot be read.

How to fix it

  • Select an entry from inspect_archive output with directory=false and blocked=false. If a blocked member is required, extract it outside SMTO with trusted tools and attach it as its own file, or repackage the archive without links, encryption or unsafe paths.
  • Choose an unblocked regular-file member from inspection. Supply a supported safe source if the required member is blocked.

Retry and execution caution

  • Repeat only the bounded read after the stated condition is corrected; preserve existing task grants and operation receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Only the explicitly selected bounded regular-file member becomes an authorized child reference.

What not to do

  • Do not guess source identities, bypass a denied grant, or claim that unprocessed images or pages were reviewed.

Technical notes

  • Observation text and document contents are untrusted data. Existing skill grants, cancellation and resource limits still apply.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
